## 1. Load the processed data

```{r load}
# Open the project's .Rproj file before running chunks.
# Install psych once in the Console if needed: install.packages("psych")

library(psych)

# Load the processed datasets
h1Data <- read.csv("Data/h1_processed.csv")
h2Data <- read.csv("Data/h2_processed.csv")

# Check the datasets
dim(h1Data)
dim(h2Data)

names(h1Data)
names(h2Data)

```

## 2. Look at the distribution first

```{r histogram}
# A histogram groups numerical values into intervals (bins).
# Bar height shows how many observations fall in each interval.
# Start by looking at the distribution before calculating summary statistics.

# Add readable labels to the same histogram.

# H1: Distribution of perceived constraints on leaving a relationship
hist(
  h1Data$relmob,
  main = "Distribution of perceived relationship mobility constraints",
  xlab = "Perceived constraints on leaving a relationship",
  col = "lightblue"
)

# H2: Distribution of daily social media use
hist(
  h2Data$Time_social_media,
  main = "Distribution of daily social media use",
  xlab = "Daily social media use",
  col = "lightblue"
)

# H2: Distribution of daily appearance-enhancement time
hist(
  h2Data$Appearance_time,
  main = "Distribution of daily time spent enhancing appearance",
  xlab = "Appearance-enhancement time",
  col = "lightblue"
)
```

## 3. One statistic at a time

```{r individual_statistics}
# Mean: add the scores and divide by the number of observed responses.
mean(h1Data$relmob, na.rm = TRUE)
mean(h2Data$Time_social_media, na.rm = TRUE)
mean(h2Data$Appearance_time, na.rm = TRUE)

# Median: the middle score after sorting the responses.
median(h1Data$relmob, na.rm = TRUE)
median(h2Data$Time_social_media, na.rm = TRUE)
median(h2Data$Appearance_time, na.rm = TRUE)

# Table: count how many people are in each category.
table(h1Data$Sex, useNA = "ifany")

# Range: return the minimum and maximum, rather than their difference.
range(h1Data$relmob, na.rm = TRUE)
range(h2Data$Time_social_media, na.rm = TRUE)
range(h2Data$Appearance_time, na.rm = TRUE)

# IQR: the 75th percentile minus the 25th percentile.
IQR(h1Data$relmob, na.rm = TRUE)
IQR(h2Data$Time_social_media, na.rm = TRUE)
IQR(h2Data$Appearance_time, na.rm = TRUE)
```

## 4. Standardize a variable

```{r standardize}
# scale() uses z = (original score - mean) / standard deviation by default.
# Keep the original commitment scores and store the standardized values separately.
# scale() returns a matrix; as.numeric() makes a simple numeric column.

# Standardize daily social media use
h2Data$Social_media_z <- as.numeric(
  scale(h2Data$Time_social_media)
)

# Standardize daily appearance-enhancement time
h2Data$Appearance_time_z <- as.numeric(
  scale(h2Data$Appearance_time)
)

# Check standardized means and standard deviations
mean(h2Data$Social_media_z, na.rm = TRUE)
sd(h2Data$Social_media_z, na.rm = TRUE)

mean(h2Data$Appearance_time_z, na.rm = TRUE)
sd(h2Data$Appearance_time_z, na.rm = TRUE)

# Standardized scores have mean approximately 0 and standard deviation 1.
```

## 5. Covariance and correlation

```{r association}
# Covariance describes whether two variables tend to move together.
# Positive: higher values tend to occur together. Negative: higher values tend to accompany lower values.
# Its size depends on the units and is not restricted to -1 through 1.

# Covariance between social media use and appearance-enhancement time
cov(
  h2Data$Time_social_media,
  h2Data$Appearance_time,
  use = "complete.obs")


# Pearson correlation expresses a linear association on a -1 to 1 scale.

# Pearson correlation between the two variables
cor(
  h2Data$Time_social_media,
  h2Data$Appearance_time,
  use = "complete.obs"
)


# Select numerical variables only; do not include participant IDs or category codes.

h2CorData <- h2Data[, c(
  "Time_social_media",
  "Appearance_time"
)]


# A correlation matrix gives the correlation for each pair of columns.

cor(h2CorData, use = "complete.obs")

# The diagonal is 1 because each variable is correlated with itself.
```

## 6. Several statistics at once

```{r combined_summaries}
# summary() reports minimum, quartiles, median, mean, maximum, and missing counts when present.

# H1: Summary of perceived constraints on leaving a relationship
summary(h1Data$relmob)

# H2: Summary of social media use and appearance-enhancement time
summary(h2CorData)


# psych::describe() reports n, mean, SD, median, minimum, maximum, range width (max minus min), skewness, kurtosis, and other summaries.
# However it does not report every statistic above: compute IQR, cov(), and cor() separately.

# H1: Descriptive statistics by gender
psych::describeBy(
  h1Data$relmob,
  group = h1Data$Sex
)

# H2: Descriptive statistics for both H2 variables
psych::describe(h2CorData)

```

```{r codebooks}
compact_codebook(h1Data_complete)
compact_codebook(h2Data_complete)
```
